title: Agreement & RegisterRef — shared definitions used by the understanding/* family
description: Reused by understanding/seal's request payload and by its understanding/seal:countered error details, so the same Agreement shape backs both an original proposal and a counter-proposal without being defined twice.

RegisterRef.title: RegisterRef
RegisterRef.description: A resolvable, version-identified, hash-pinned pointer to one register of the agreement. The same `{ uri, version, digestMultibase }` shape as understanding/offer's termsRef and as the governance-framework reference the companion Verifiable Trust Infrastructure specification places in a DID document (VTI-KEY-052: a `GovernanceFramework` service whose `serviceEndpoint` is the `uri`, with `version` and `digestMultibase` members).

uri.description: Where this register of the agreement can be resolved.

version.description: The publisher's own version label for the resolved document.

digestMultibase.description: The multibase-encoded multihash of the resolved document's bytes at this `version`, so a party that fetches `uri` later can confirm it is the same content this agreement named.

mediaType.description: The media type of the resolved document.

name.description: A consistent, transparent name for this agreement, meaningful to a non-specialist — IEEE 7012-2025 §4.3. A separate version member is not carried: §4.3's own note permits a release date in place of a version number, and `effectiveFrom` already serves that role.

rosterItems.description: The agreed terms, as identifiers into the roster the grounding understanding/offer response's termsRef names. MUST be drawn from that same roster — see understanding/seal's Authorization section.

legalRef.description: OPTIONAL pointer to the agreement's canonical legal-register text.

machineReadableRef.description: OPTIONAL pointer to the agreement's machine-readable register (for example JSON-LD).

effectiveUntil.description: OPTIONAL. When the agreement lapses on its own terms, absent a separate termination.

counterAgreement.description: The second party's single alternative agreement, per IEEE 7012-2025 §5.3.1(b). MUST NOT be carried in reply to a request that itself carries `respondsTo`.
